messages:
nora: @channel quick heads-up — running a multi-region preemptible wargame tomorrow 08:30 PT. Goal: validate our mixed-capacity strategy (spot + on-demand GPUs across regions), exercise interruption handling, and confirm autoscaler + rollout behavior under pressure. I pasted a short runbook below. Ack and call out any blockers.
alex: ack. I'll own the chaos runner and spot eviction injector. Will produce a short script to pick nodes by capacity label.
jun: can we add a networking partition case? last time small route flap caused control-plane reconnections and a bunch of restart churn.
maddy: +1. I'll build dashboard panels for per-model token latency, queue length, node eviction rate, and pending pods. Also add a 'cold cache' metric for KV cache hit-rate.
ryan: what are our success criteria so SRE and product know when to stop the drill?
nora: initial success criteria: 1) priority-tier 95th latency stays <300ms (during first 60s after evictions), 2) >99.9% requests served (no silent drops), 3) autoscaler returns to target capacity within 90s after each wave, 4) no cross-region data-plane degradation (model outputs consistent). If any criterion fails we abort and collect traces.
eva: do we want to include KMS timeouts for Private customers? I've seen KMS-induced spikes cascade into retry storms.
alex: yeah include KMS delay simulation as an optional subtest. For evictions we'll use this command to drain nodes (example):
```
# pick node from label gpu-type=rtx-40
kubectl drain node/<node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --force
```
alex: eviction injector will annotate nodes with test-run:<id> and then drain. Will run 5 random single-node drains, 2 region-level waves (30% of spot pool), and a final mixed-capacity wave where we remove on-demand nodes first.
eviction-bot: scheduled chaos job created: wargame-2026-03-19-08:30PT, waves=5, owners=[alex]
maddy: canary traffic plan: shift 20% of read-only requests to backup region during the second wave. Also will reduce batch sizes for the canary route to highlight latency-sensitive failures.
jun: reminder: set the model fallback chain so heavy models fall back to trimmed quantized variants — helpful to maintain throughput during capacity drops.
ryan: ops checklist snippet to collect when an issue happens:
```
kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide --selector='app=redwood-runtime' > /tmp/pods.txt
kubectl logs -l app=redwood-runtime -n runtime --since=10m --tail=300 > /tmp/runtime-logs.txt
# collect autoscaler metrics
kubectl get hpa -n runtime -o yaml > /tmp/hpa.yaml
```
maddy: note for dashboards — add a panel that shows eviction rate per node group and a separate one for queue growth for priority vs. background traffic.
eva: prepping KMS replay harnesses and a mode that injects 500-2k ms KMS delays. I'll toggle that only in Private-sim tests.
nora: assignable roles: alex=chaos scripts & orchestrator; maddy=dashboards/canary traffic; jun=network partition and runbook executor; ryan=logs + postmortem lead; eva=KMS & private deployment sim. If anyone wants to swap call it out now.
alex: I'll also capture GCP/AWS spot eviction metadata (instanceId, terminationTime) and push as annotations to our traces.
ryan: small reminder — make sure autoscaler controller has an increased cache TTL for node group lookups to avoid thundering lookups during waves.
jun: plan to run a 10s UDP loss partition (iptables in test VPC) for one wave to see grpc retries behavior.
maddy: quick config note: set local KV cache TTL to 2s for the cold-cache wave so we can measure warm-up effect explicitly.
nora: ok final call: if no blockers we'll go ahead. Postmortem template and runbook are here: <link-to-runbook>. Please add the runbook step owners inline and include the warm-up checklist. :thumbsup:
alex: ack, will share the chaos script and invocations in this thread when ready.
eviction-bot: run queued: wargame-2026-03-19-08:30PT — notify @channel 15m prior.
maddy: one last ask — can we reserve a small number of on-demand GPUs (2-3) as a safety pool to validate cold start times if everything else is gone?
nora: yes reserve 3 on-demand in each region as a safety pool. Add that to runbook.
ryan: copying the autoscaler recovery expectation to the runbook: recover to target within 90s or mark SLO violation.
eva: prepping KMS logs collection steps and a simple analysis script to correlate KMS latency spikes with retry rate.
alex: shipping initial scripts in ~2 hours.
nora: thanks all, see you in the war room channel tomorrow. Keep any last-minute blockers here.
